functional_semantics.triton: out = where(x_keep != 0, x / (1 - p), 0) with x_keep an INPUT mask (impl_triton.py L21-23); no RNG anywhere in the file.
functional_semantics.cutile: out = x_keep * x * (1/(1-p)) with x_keep an input mask (impl_cutile.py L24-26, scale on host L37); no RNG.
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py L5 ((x * x_keep) * (1/(1-p))). The mask is drawn by the generator (tensors.py L189) as exact 0/1 values in x's dtype; run() is deterministic on all sides. Select-on-nonzero vs multiply-by-mask coincide for 0/1 masks.

stages.triton: One element-wise kernel over a 1-D grid: load x and x_keep (L21-22), compute (L23), store (L24).
stages.cutile: One element-wise kernel over a 1-D grid: load x and x_keep (L24-25), compute (L26), store (L27).
stages.note: Single pass, no intermediates on either side.

reduction_scan_sort.note: Purely element-wise; no RNG stream to advance.

precision.triton: x / (1 - p) with p a runtime fp32 scalar, so fp16/bf16 x is promoted to fp32 for the division; select via tl.where on x_keep.to(int1); one implicit rounding to x.dtype at tl.store (L23-24).
precision.cutile: x and x_keep cast to fp32 (L24-25), product x_keep * x * scale with scale = 1/(1-p) computed on the host (L37, L26), one explicit rounding to x.dtype (L26).
precision.note: Both evaluate the rescale in fp32 with exactly one rounding to the output dtype. Division by (1-p) versus multiplication by the host-computed reciprocal differs by at most one fp32 ulp (identical for the configured p = 0.5, where the factor is exactly 2) and the mask is applied as a select versus a multiply; neither changes the accumulation path or the rounding point, so the contract permits either form.

preprocessing.triton: torch.empty_like output (L41); n_elements (L42); p passed as a kernel scalar (L45, L50).
preprocessing.note: No casts, copies or cached state; computing 1/(1-p) on the host is scalar metadata.

mutation.triton: No input written; fresh output per call (L41).
mutation.cutile: No input written; fresh output per call (L35).

fq_boundary.note: One read of x, one read of x_keep (same dtype as x) and one write of the output match the single kernel's compulsory traffic on both sides. The mask is a pre-generated input, so no RNG cost exists inside the boundary; no preprocessing or prepacked input exists.
